overall_status: internally derived stability theorem and calibration obstruction; prior-art bounded, not externally reviewed or novelty-cleared

claims.statement: For a weighted complex projective 2-design (u_j,p_j) in C^d, d>=2, physical rows a_j=t_j u_j with p_j=t_j^4/S and S=sum_j t_j^4, and raw observations y_j=t_j^2(1+gamma_j)|v_j^*x|^2+eta_j, where ||x||<=R, ||v_j||=1, max_j min_phase||v_j-phase*u_j||<=delta and max_j|gamma_j|<=gamma<1, the nominal dual-frame inverse Xhat=sum_j(t_j^2 y_j/S)[d(d+1)Pi_j-dI] obeys ||Xhat-xx*||_F <= R^2[sqrt(2)gamma+(1+gamma)(2sqrt(d+1)delta+sqrt(d(d+1))delta^2)] + sqrt(d(d+1)/S)||eta||_2.
assumptions: positive p_j sum to one and sum p_j Pi_j tensor Pi_j=(I+F)/[d(d+1)]
direction error is projective chordal error between unit vectors
gain error is multiplicative intensity gain, not amplitude gain
claims.status: internally derived from the exact frame identity; not externally reviewed
claims.source_pointers: Proof is reproduced in the report: weighted design gives F_p(H)=(H+Tr(H)I)/d(d+1) and ||F_p^{-1}A_p^*||=sqrt(d(d+1)); rank-one design moments give sum p z=||x||^2/d and sum p z^2=2||x||^4/[d(d+1)]; row direction perturbations obey ||ztilde-z||_p<=2delta R^2/sqrt(d)+delta^2 R^2.
claims.novelty_boundary: The noiseless projective-design inverse is prior art (Levenshtein/Scott; Balan-Bodmann-Casazza-Edidin). General frame perturbation and phase retrieval total-least-squares under sensing-vector/data errors are also prior art. This is a transparent specialization to the weighted lifted inverse and stated gain/projector/readout interface, not a general new phase retrieval stability theorem.
claims.costs: m scalar intensity channels; raw output precision enters through ||eta||2/sqrt(S); relative intensity gain calibration needs O(epsilon/R^2) accuracy and projective direction accuracy O(epsilon/[R^2 sqrt(d)]) for target lifted Frobenius error epsilon, up to the displayed constants. Calibration-shot counts require an external calibrator/noise model.
claims.falsifier: A weighted 2-design and admissible x, gains, projective row perturbations or eta violating the displayed deterministic inequality; or an algebra error in the canonical inverse norm or projector perturbation estimate.
claims.next_gate: Independent frame-theory derivation review and a finite numerical test on a Jasper-Mixon Sidon/Bodmann-Haas instance against lifted OLS/GLS and rank-one raw least squares.

claims.statement: When physical row amplitudes satisfy t_j^4=Sp_j, the weighted-design inverse is exactly the Moore-Penrose ordinary least-squares estimator for all raw lifted rows A_t(H)_j=t_j^2 Tr(Pi_j H). Its frame operator has scalar eigenvalue S/d and traceless eigenvalue S/[d(d+1)], hence condition number sqrt(d+1). Under independent zero-mean raw-output noise with variances sigma_j^2, its exact Frobenius MSE around its mean is K_d sum_j t_j^4 sigma_j^2/S^2, K_d=d^2(d^2+d-1).
assumptions: the lifted Hermitian variable is unrestricted for the OLS comparison
noise coordinates are independent and have finite stated variances for the MSE formula
claims.status: algebraically derived; Gauss-Markov consequence is standard; not externally reviewed
claims.source_pointers: A_t^*A_t=S F_p; the displayed canonical dual formula equals (A_t^*A_t)^-1 A_t^* y. D_j=d(d+1)Pi_j-dI has squared Frobenius norm d^2(d^2+d-1), independent of j.
claims.novelty_boundary: This identifies the closed form with raw-data OLS; it is a control result and not a novelty claim. Heteroskedastic known-noise GLS and rank-one constrained LS are equally informed controls and can improve or use the same data more effectively.
claims.costs: Same m raw scalar readings and the same rows as the closed-form inverse. Generic dense accumulation costs O(md^2); the Jasper-Mixon character structure admits an O(|G| log |G|+d^2) finite-group FFT implementation, assuming group representation/FFT is supplied.
claims.falsifier: A failure of A_t^*A_t=S F_p or a discrepancy between the formula and the raw OLS pseudoinverse on an exact design.
claims.next_gate: Reproduce the identity and covariance formula in a numerical d=2 and a small Sidon construction implementation; separately benchmark GLS under specified heteroskedasticity.

claims.statement: If signal norm is unknown and a common intensity gain g is only known to lie in [1-gamma,1+gamma], then noiseless intensity data cannot uniformly recover X=xx* over ||x||<=R to Frobenius error below gamma R^2/(1+gamma), regardless of the sensing rows or their count.
assumptions: unknown signal norm over the radius-R ball
claims.source_pointers: Instances (1-gamma,R^2 vv*) and (1+gamma,[(1-gamma)/(1+gamma)]R^2 vv*) induce identical data and have Frobenius distance 2 gamma R^2/(1+gamma).
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary scale/gain confounding; no novelty claim. Does not apply when signal norm is known exactly or only the normalized direction is a target.
claims.costs: More phase-retrieval samples do not break the ambiguity. An independent gain calibration or known signal norm is necessary.
claims.falsifier: A decoder that distinguishes the two parameter pairs from identical deterministic observations without side information.
claims.next_gate: Include gain-reference acquisition and its uncertainty in any physical experimental protocol.

claims.statement: For the Jasper-Mixon near-minimal Sidon/Bodmann-Haas weighted design with d=|S| and N=|G|, normalized character and coordinate weights are p_chi=d/[N(d+1)] and p_r=1/[d(d+1)], with ratio N/d^2. In their N=d^2+O(d^1.525) regime, max_j|m p_j-1|=O(d^-0.475), so those weights are asymptotically near-uniform.
assumptions: theorem 7 Bodmann-Haas construction in Jasper-Mixon arXiv:2501.14938v1
dense Sidon-set parameter regime yielding N=d^2+O(d^1.525)
claims.source_pointers: Theorem 7 proof lines 132-134 gives unnormalized character weights d^2/(2N), coordinate weights 1/2; Theorem 4 and section 3 give the near-minimal cardinality bound.
claims.novelty_boundary: A normalization/cost interpretation of the source construction, not a new design theorem. General sparse-in-group Sidon choices can have a different weight ratio; the claim is specifically about the near-minimal regime.
claims.costs: m=N+d=d^2+O(d^1.525) scalar channels; no sampling or exposure reduction follows from the weights. Equal-scale unit rows with weighted processing have variance K_d sigma^2 sum p_j^2; row-amplitude coding makes the formula raw OLS under homoscedastic raw noise.
claims.falsifier: Recompute the normalized weights or exhibit an allowed near-minimal Sidon parameter sequence with nonvanishing max_j|m p_j-1|.
claims.next_gate: Use the exact finite Sidon parameters in a reproducible weight/noise/FFT simulation; do not infer Poisson dose from additive noise.

cost_ledger.acquisition: m scalar intensity channels; the base theorem assumes all rows measured once; repeated-exposure formula is in CYCLE2_REPORT.md
cost_ledger.response_precision: mb bits for b-bit raw outputs; deterministic quantizer bound and sufficient b are stated in CYCLE2_REPORT.md
cost_ledger.calibration: Sufficient relative-gain/projector precision is quantified; calibration shot counts are UNKNOWN without a reference and noise model
cost_ledger.computation: O(md^2) generic accumulation, or O(|G| log |G|+d^2) with a supplied Jasper-Mixon finite-group FFT representation
cost_ledger.representation: Dense lifted X uses d^2 real values; a rank-one factor uses 2d-1 real values up to global phase, but noisy factorization stability is not established here
cost_ledger.physical_noise: No Poisson/shot-noise or detector exposure model is assumed

prior_art: Levenshtein/Scott reconstruction identity, presented in Balan-Bodmann-Casazza-Edidin Theorem 3.4 and Remark 3.5
Alharbi et al. 2022/2023 quantitative phase-retrieval frame perturbations
Gupta-Dokmanic 2021 Total Least Squares Phase Retrieval handles sensing-vector and measurement errors

finite_checks.scope: d=2, G=Z_3, Sidon set S={0,1}; five-row Jasper-Mixon/Bodmann-Haas weighted design. Moment identity error 1.665e-16; explicit weighted inverse/raw OLS max-entry gap 3.553e-15; one randomized gain/projector/noise fixture had matrix error 0.113801 below theorem bound 0.322494.
